chunks: Al-Fadl, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Khalid ibn Abi 'Imarah, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

We mentioned the Qaim (peace be upon him) and those of our companions who died waiting for him. He (peace be upon him) said to us: When he rises, he will come to the believer in his grave, and it will be said to him: O you! Your Imam has appeared. If you wish to join him, join him; and if you wish to remain in the honor of your Lord, remain.

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Rising One, a title for Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him)
key_terms.يَنْتَظِرُهُ: Waiting for him (referring to the reappearance)

ai.seo_question: What happens to believers waiting for the Imam in their graves when he reappears?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the unique spiritual status of the *Mutahabbun* (those who love and await the Imam) during the Major Occultation, portraying the grave not merely as a place of waiting but as a realm of active anticipation. The choice offered—joining the Imam immediately or remaining in divine honor—underscores the Shia eschatological view that the Imam’s reappearance is the pivotal event that resolves the state of *Barzakh* for his followers, bridging the gap between death and resurrection.
